prompt-logging-hook.name: Prompt Logging Hook
prompt-logging-hook.description: UserPromptSubmit hook that auto-logs every developer prompt to their own prompts/<name>.jsonl (author, timestamp, prompt text) for hackathon tracking. Registered in .claude/settings.json; delegates to scripts/log-prompt.mjs. prompts.jsonl at the repo root is a frozen historical archive from before the per-contributor split and no longer receives new writes; a leftover unresolved merge conflict in it (from an old `git stash pop`) was resolved in place on 2026-09-05.

authenticated.name: Authenticated
authenticated.description: Valid signed-in user session required. Enforced by verifying a signed JWT (Authorization: Bearer <token>) issued by #auth-service on signup/login; the `sub` claim is the user id. Backed by the `users` table (email + bcrypt password_hash). Replaces the earlier Bearer=userId hackathon stand-in.

checkout-authorized.name: Checkout Authorized
checkout-authorized.description: Per-user spending-policy check (per-tx/daily USDC caps) plus an explicit !checkout-confirmed signal from the user for amounts above the auto-approve threshold. Runs after ^authenticated, before any wallet transfer is submitted. The cap check and the order insert run inside one Postgres transaction holding a per-user advisory lock (#orders-service.reserveOrder), so two concurrent requests near the cap can't both pass the check before either commits. The same call also dedups client resubmissions (a client-supplied idempotency token, or a short window keyed on user+sku+quantity+amount) so a double-click/retry can't create a second order or a second real Circle transfer, and runs the (currently no-op) Circle Policy Engine hook — see .paradigm/specs/wallet-checkout.md "Hardening".

agent-authorized.name: Agent Authorized
agent-authorized.description: Valid agent grant required. A signed JWT with audience "agent" (Authorization: Bearer <grant>) minted by #agent-route POST /agent/grant for a signed-in human. Distinct from ^authenticated (a human user token) so an agent cannot use the ungated human /checkout, and a human token cannot start an agent purchase.

personhood-verified.name: Personhood Verified
personhood-verified.description: Live proof-of-personhood (World ID Selfie Check / Face Auth) tied to a specific agent-initiated order. #agent-route creates a pending order + a single-use, short-TTL verification session; no money moves until the human completes the selfie (#verify-route). Currently mocked; the real World ID proof verification swaps in at #verification-service. This is the agent path's step-up, replacing the human path's !checkout-confirmed.

webhook-signature-verified.name: Webhook Signature Verified
webhook-signature-verified.description: Verifies Circle's X-Circle-Signature / X-Circle-Key-Id headers. Used instead of ^authenticated on webhook routes, which have no user session.

grant-scope-valid.name: Grant Scope Valid
grant-scope-valid.description: App-level "session key" check for agent-initiated orders only (#agent-grants-service). At settlement (#verify-route's settleVerifiedSession, right before executePayment()) the order's originating grant is re-checked: not revoked, not past its own (shorter-than-the-JWT) expiry, destination matches merchantPayoutAddress(), and the amount is within that grant's per-tx cap and rolling-24h cap — in addition to, not instead of, ^checkout-authorized's app-wide caps. #agent-route also does an early, best-effort version of the revoked/expired check at POST /agent/checkout so a doomed order isn't reserved, but the settlement-time check is authoritative since a grant can be revoked in between. Human orders have no agent grant and are unaffected. This is deliberately NOT an on-chain session key — see .paradigm/specs/wallet-checkout.md "Session-scoped agent grants" for the deferred on-chain (ERC-4337 + Smart Contract Account) follow-up.

ledger-confirmed.name: Ledger Confirmed
ledger-confirmed.description: For a user with an enrolled Ledger device only (#ledger-confirm-service) — everyone else is unaffected. A physical Ledger signs an EIP-712 typed-data struct over {orderId, sku, quantity, amountUsdc, destinationAddress, nonce, expiresAt, chainId} binding the approval to the specific STORED order row; verification always reconstructs the hash server-side from that row, never from caller-echoed fields, and resolves the approval (and consumes its nonce) atomically with checking it, so a resubmission of the same order's idempotency key reuses one approval rather than requiring a second. Fails closed: denial/expiry/replay marks the order failed/denied, never left 'pending'. For a human checkout above the $10 auto-approve threshold this REPLACES the spoofable checkoutConfirmed boolean; for an agent-initiated purchase it runs alongside (not instead of) ^personhood-verified and ^grant-scope-valid at settlement. LEDGER_CONFIRM_MODE=mock (default) is a click-through stand-in for demoing without hardware; a real device plus the companion approver process is a follow-up — see .paradigm/specs/wallet-checkout.md "Ledger confirmation gate".
